subject: Hygiene Development
content: Infection control prevents spread of infectious diseases in healthcare and community settings. Key practices: hand hygiene (wash with soap/water or alcohol-based sanitizer), personal protective equipment (gloves, masks, gowns), respiratory etiquette (cover coughs/sneezes with elbow), cleaning and disinfection (surfaces, equipment), waste disposal (sharps containers, biohazard bags), isolation (separating infected people). Chain of infection: infectious agent → reservoir (where germ lives) → portal of exit → transmission → portal of entry → susceptible host. Breaking any link prevents infection. Nigerian hospitals follow infection control protocols. At home: wash hands, clean surfaces, handle food safely, stay home when sick. Infection control protects vulnerable people: elderly, pregnant, newborns, sick patients.
summary: Infection control prevents disease spread. Practices: hand hygiene, PPE, respiratory etiquette, cleaning, waste disposal, isolation. Break chain of infection.

subject: Hygiene Development
content: WASH stands for Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene. Safe water: treated, boiled, or filtered water prevents waterborne diseases (cholera, typhoid). Sanitation: proper disposal of human waste through toilets, latrines, sewage systems prevents contamination of water sources. Hygiene: handwashing with soap, bathing, cleaning clothes prevents disease transmission. WASH is a global priority because millions lack access to clean water and toilets. In Nigeria, many communities lack piped water. Solutions: boreholes, wells (covered), water treatment (chlorine tablets, boiling), VIP latrines (ventilated improved pit), handwashing stations. Open defecation spreads disease. Nigeria is working to end open defecation by 2030. Everyone can practice WASH: boil water, use toilet, wash hands, keep environment clean.
summary: WASH = Water, Sanitation, Hygiene. Safe water prevents waterborne diseases. Proper toilets prevent contamination. Handwashing prevents transmission. Nigeria working to end open defecation.

subject: Hygiene Development
content: Vector control manages organisms that transmit diseases. Vectors: mosquitoes (malaria, dengue, yellow fever), rats (Lassa fever, leptospirosis), flies (typhoid, cholera), ticks (Lyme disease). Malaria prevention: sleep under insecticide-treated bed nets (ITNs), use window screens, remove standing water (where mosquitoes breed), use insect repellent, indoor residual spraying (IRS). Rat control: store food in closed containers, seal holes in walls, use traps, keep environment clean. Fly control: cover food, dispose of rubbish properly, use screens. Nigeria has high malaria burden; vector control saves lives. The National Malaria Elimination Program distributes bed nets. Everyone can help: empty containers, clear bushes, fix holes, dispose trash properly. Vector control prevents outbreaks.
summary: Vector control manages disease-transmitting organisms: mosquitoes (malaria), rats (Lassa), flies (typhoid). Malaria prevention: bed nets, remove standing water, screens, repellent.

subject: Hygiene Development
content: Public health emergency preparedness means planning for disease outbreaks, natural disasters, or other health crises. Steps: risk assessment (identify potential emergencies: epidemics, floods, chemical spills), planning (create response protocols, assign roles), stockpiling (medical supplies, PPE, medicines), training (health workers, volunteers), communication (public alerts, health education), coordination (government, NGOs, international partners). Nigerian experiences: COVID-19 pandemic, Ebola preparedness, Lassa fever outbreaks, cholera during floods, monkeypox. Community preparedness: have emergency contacts, prepare supply kit (water, food, mask, medicines, flashlight), know evacuation routes, follow official instructions, avoid misinformation. The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) coordinates responses. Preparedness saves lives.
summary: Public health emergency preparedness: plan for outbreaks, disasters. Steps: risk assessment, planning, stockpiling, training, communication, coordination. NCDC coordinates Nigerian response.
